earlier_scan.note: Extinct W Tucanoan; only Koch-Gruenberg/Martius wordlists per Glottolog, no phonology

sources.citation: lexibank/chacontukanoan: CLDF dataset derived from Chacon 2014 'A revised proposal of Proto-Tukanoan consonants and Tukanoan family classification' (IJAL 80.3).
sources.note: lists Kueretu (ID KUE, glottocode cure1236) among 16 varieties; lexical/cognate data only, no prosodic annotation.

sources.citation: Martius, Carl Friedrich Philipp von. 1867. Beiträge zur Ethnographie und Sprachenkunde Amerika's zumal Brasiliens, Bd. II: Glossaria linguarum Brasiliensium. Leipzig: Fleischer. 'Coretú' pp. 164-166.
sources.note: Bare Latin-Coretú wordlist (footnote: taken by Martius from chief Pachicúh at S. João do Príncipe on the Japurá); diacritics present but no remarks on accent. The separate 'Curetú' list p. 284f (after Wallace) is Yupúa, with Martius's own footnote doubting its identity.

sources.citation: Chacon, Thiago Costa & Johann-Mattis List. 2015. Improved computational models of sound change shed light on the history of the Tukanoan languages. Journal of Language Relationship 13(3): 177-204.
sources.note: Kueretu (Kue) included as a Western Tukanoan variety from Koch-Grünberg's data; discusses consonant changes (*dz > j, *ts > t, t > n /~V_V in Kueretu); nothing on stress or accent in Kueretu.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1914. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete (Fortsetzung): Desána, Yupúa, Yahúna, Kueretú. Anthropos 9: 812-832.
sources.note: Four-column comparative wordlist; Kueretú forms carry an acute accent per item on varying syllables (p. 812: siámelako 'Zunge', sikoméo 'Nase', siakókia 'Auge', sikiatílo 'Ohr', stróho 'Kopf', strohóre 'Kopfhaar', sikiakómeno 'Schulter', simahúmpu 'Hand'); footnotes concern Yahúna/Yupúa segments only; no statement about accent placement.

sources.citation: Koch-Grünberg, Theodor. 1913. Betóya-Sprachen Nordwestbrasiliens und der angrenzenden Gebiete [I]. Anthropos 8: 944-977.
sources.note: General 'Lautlehre' (p. 948) for all his Betoya vocabularies lists only the diacritic: 'á Wortakzent.' (acute = word accent, marked per item); 'Bemerkungen zu den einzelnen Sprachen' (p. 949) has no Kueretú entry; p. 947 says the Kueretú list was taken March-April 1905 on the lower Apaporís; p. 950 names Martius 1867 II:164ff as the only earlier Kueretú source and says Wallace's 'Curetu' is really Yupúa. No stress rule.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record cure1236 'Kueretu' and its 5 references (bibtex saved).
